transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-09
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Anna (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lisa (ClearSight PM), Mateo (ClearSight ML), Priya K. (ClearSight SRE), Tom (ClearSight Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, optional): Customer wants to validate cost/latency tradeoffs for streaming conversational scoring and batch embedding generation. Focus on harness integration and who owns which scripts.

00:00 Anna (AE): ok hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call. we wanted to use today's time to pin down the benchmark plan and who owns the customer-side scripts.
00:22 Lisa (Customer PM): yep thanks, appreciate you fitting us in. our main goal is to prove we can hit 200 concurrent sessions at p95 < 450ms for the chat scoring flow and keep token cost under $0.0008 per token equivalent, roughly.
00:38 Carlos (SE): got it. just to clarify when you say "chat scoring" is that streaming partial responses to the UI or non-stream where you wait for final output?
00:50 Lisa: both. we have a live UX that streams tokens for a better snappy feel, and a batch offline scorer for nightly reranks. we want both represented.
01:05 Mateo (ML): and we want the streaming test to include KV cache warmup — sessions that interact over 6 turns average, about 350 tokens per session total.
01:20 Priya S. (Redwood SE): perfect context. can you confirm typical prompt size distribution and tokens per call? even rough numbers help us pick model variant and batching targets.
01:33 Mateo: most prompts are short — median 40 tokens, 90th percentile 260 tokens, with occasional long queries hitting ~1k tokens. average response tokens about 120.
01:46 Anna: ok note that. for the benchmark harness we recommend two main vectors: streaming conversational (live path) and non-stream batch scoring (nightly rerank). we'll set separate load generators for each.
02:01 Tom (Procurement): hi quick question — will these tests touch any PII? we need to be sure about scope for legal.
02:10 Lisa: all prompts will be anonymized; Mateo will sanitize and send samples.
02:15 Anna: great. security wise we will run in Redwood staging, you can use a short-lived API key and we support VPC egress allowlisting if needed. also we can enable customer-managed KMS for any artifacts if required.
02:33 Priya K. (SRE): for streaming tests we need to confirm if the harness uses HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming or WebSocket; our infra is tuned for ws but we can adapt. which does Redwood support?
02:48 Carlos: Redwood supports both streaming over HTTP chunked responses and a WebSocket-based stream adapter on dedicated. for hosted staging we usually use chunked HTTP streaming. small transcription note: sometimes chunk boundaries look like micro-bursts in the metrics.
03:06 Lisa: can you outline what you expect from us vs what Redwood will provide for the harness integration?
03:12 Anna: yes, here's an ownership split — Redwood provides the harness runner, load shaping controls, metrics capture (latency percentiles, token throughput, error rate), and example customer-script format. Customer provides a sanitized prompt corpus, authentication details for the temp account, and any session affinity rules (cookie or session id patterns). we'll collaborate on the YAML config that maps prompt files to concurrency curves.
03:36 Mateo: on customer scripts: our current harness is in python and uses a producer-consumer pattern — we can adapt but prefer to reuse what we have. will Redwood accept customer-provided scripts?
03:47 Carlos: yes. we have a pluggable loader — you can drop a script that implements a simple interface (send_request, parse_response). we also provided a node example and a python example link in the playbook. we'll send the interface spec.
04:03 Anna: action item — we'll post the harness contract and a minimal example script to the shared drive after this call.
04:10 Lisa: good. about metrics: we want p50/p90/p95 and also tokens/sec per model and cost per 1M tokens extrapolated. can the harness compute cost estimates?
04:24 Carlos: harness will emit tokens and model usage per request; cost calc is a simple post-process — we can give you the formula and a spreadsheet to plug in Redwood staging rates vs expected production discounts.
04:36 Mateo: another important bit: for streaming we need to measure end-to-end UI perceived latency (time to first token) and also steady-state token latency. can we instrument client-side timing?
04:48 Priya S.: yes we recommend adding a client-side tracing header; the harness and Redwood runtime will propagate and attach server-side timings to the same trace id. often the UI measurement is done by the customer and we correlate with the server spans.
05:03 Tom: timeline — how long will a full benchmark run take? we have a decision window in early Aug.
05:12 Anna: recommended plan: 1) Week of 7/14 — handshake, script drop and config; 2) Week of 7/21 — dry-run 2-hour window with low concurrency to validate instrumentation; 3) Week of 7/28 — 6-hour full run covering peak curves and warmup; 4) Week of 8/4 — analysis and readout. that's tight but doable for an August decision.
05:36 Lisa: ok that works. do you need dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) or can staging simulate production concurrency?
05:45 Carlos: for initial sizing staging is fine up to N concurrent sessions; if you want guaranteed isolation we can spin up a small dedicated test pool for the run. dedicated gives more consistent p95 but costs more. we'll surface both numbers.
06:02 Mateo: how do we represent session warm starts vs cold starts in the harness? we care because cache priming changes cost significantly.
06:12 Priya S.: harness will run trials with cold-starts (no KV cache primed) and warm-starts (run a priming pass per session simulating N previous turns). We'll include a separate experiment to measure steady-state after 15 minutes of continuous load.
06:27 Lisa: about the customer script format — is the interface synchronous blocking calls or async stream handlers?
06:34 Carlos: both supported. for streaming you'll provide an async handler that yields packets; for non-stream batch you implement a sync send_request. sample interfaces in the playbook include pseudo-code.
06:47 Mateo: any guidance on concurrency shaping? our production bursts are spiky — 1k sessions over 10s, but average is 150 concurrent. we need the harness to reproduce that tail behavior.
06:58 Carlos: the harness supports custom curves — you can define a burst pattern. we'll also add a stochastic arrival generator to simulate realistic spikes.
07:12 Anna: good catch. another important test is token-level batching impact on latency — we need to run experiments with batching disabled, with 4ms batching window, and with 20ms window to see cost vs latency tradeoff.
07:29 Lisa: can Redwood show the internal batching counts (how many requests were batched together)?
07:34 Carlos: yes, the runtime emits batching metrics — batch size histogram and wait time. we'll include that in the runbook.
07:42 Mateo: for non-stream embedding jobs (nightly rerank) we will send large batches of up to 10k texts. what's the recommended approach? chunk into 1k batches?
07:53 Priya S.: we recommend chunking to ~512-1024 items per batch depending on token length. we'll test a few configurations to find the sweet spot. also quantized model variants may reduce cost with minimal quality loss for embeddings.
08:09 Tom: procurement question: will the staging billable tokens show up on our trial invoice? we need cost visibility.
08:16 Anna: staging runs will be accounted but we can provide a sandbox billing view and capped spend. we'll agree on a spend cap before the full run.
08:23 Lisa: great. any known gotchas?
08:26 Carlos: small ones — streaming metrics sometimes have high variance if the network path has microbursts; we recommend doing multiple repetition windows and discarding first N minutes as warmup. also align time sync for client and server to compute accurate first-byte lat.
08:45 Mateo: on the topic of models, can Redwood run both 7B quantized and a 13B float baseline so we can compare?
08:53 Carlos: yes we'll provide a 7B int8 qual variant and a 13B baseline. discuss quality regression thresholds; you mentioned earlier that automated evals should flag >1% drop on key prompts.
09:05 Lisa: yes success includes maintaining our quality baseline (measured by our scoring script) within 1% of current production for core intents.
09:14 Anna: ok we'll include eval pass where we run your scoring script across sampled prompts before/after model switch. please provide the scoring code.
09:25 Mateo: we'll provide it, python unit test style.
09:29 Tom: procurement — can you provide a short SOW and a costs estimate for a dedicated run?
09:35 Anna: yes we'll send an SOW template plus the estimated cost delta for dedicated vs hosted testing.
09:41 Carlos: small note: streaming over WebSocket on dedicated gives slightly lower time-to-first-byte in our tests due to persistent connections; we'll show both.
09:55 Lisa: ok recap — you will provide harness contract, example scripts, schedule sheet, and provison staging keys. we will sanitize prompts, provide scoring script, and confirm network rules.
10:08 Anna: perfect. action items and timeline are captured in the shared spreadsheet. we'll follow up by EOD with links.
10:18 End of call.

Attachments / shared links mentioned: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/poc-benchmark-contract.md , https://drive.redwood.com/shared/clearSight-poc/benchmark-schedule.xlsx , example scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-harness-examples

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had minor name mismatches (Priya appears twice -> Priya S. vs Priya K.). occasional punctuation errors preserved.
file_notes: POC scoping; unique focus on harness contract and ownership split; emphasizes streaming vs non-stream testing and warmup experiments. Includes clear next steps and timeline aiming for decision in early August.
